To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the FSI algorithm retrieves CO 2 columns from SCIAMACHY measurements which are of high precision ( 1%) and have a bias of <4.0%.

the FSI algorithm retrieves atmospheric CO 2 concentrations with an overall accuracy better than 4.0% and with an overall precision of 1.0%, which is sufficient to study seasonal variations of the atmospheric CO 2 distribution.

the FSI WWM-DOAS algorithm retrieves CO 2 columns with a precision of approximately 1% and a bias of less than 4% with respect to ground based FT-IR measurements and that SCIAMACHY is able to detect the seasonal cycle of CO 2 in the northern hemisphere with a precision of  0.5%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method to retrieve CO 2 from SCIAMACHY spectral measurements in the NIR and its application to the analysis of the SCIAM-ACHY CO 2 data product.
the retrieval and interpretation of atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) from SCIAMACHY measurements.
the validation of atmospheric CO 2 retrievals from SCIAMACHY using the FSI WFS DOAS algorithm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SCIAMACHYY CO 2 data set is of sufficient quality to be used as input to inverse models, though further work is required to improve the accuracy of the retrievals.
the CO 2 retrievals are of sufficient quality to allow the detection of large scale seasonal variations and to be used to validate global atmospheric transport models.
the SCIAMACH Y instrument is able to retrieve CO 2 columns with a precision of  1.0% and with an absolute uncertainty of  4.0%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SCIAMACHY is able to detect changes in atmospheric CO 2 concentrations with a precision of 1.0% and an overall bias of 4.0%.

we have demonstrated that FSI WFM DOAS is able to retrieve atmospheric CO 2 with a precision of 1% or better, and that the SCIAMACHV instrument is capable of detecting the seasonal changes in the atmospheric CO 2 distribution.
the CO 2 data set produced by the FSI retrieval is a useful and valuable data set for the study of the global CO 2 distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SCIAMACHY can be used to monitor CO 2 distributions in the Northern Hemisphere, and the FSI algorithm, in particular, is a viable retrieval option.

FSI WFM DOAS is able to retrieve CO 2 with a precision comparable to other satellite based instruments, and that the SCIAMACH Y CO 2 data are suitable for use as an input to chemistry-transport models.

SCIAMACHY is capable of retrieving atmospheric CO 2 columns with an accuracy of better than 4% and a precision of better than 1% for monthly gridded data, and that the retrieved data are of sufficient quality for use in climate research.
